name: Vietnamese (Central)
sources: Thompson, Laurence C. (1965). A Vietnamese Grammar. University of Washington Press.
Hoàng, Thị Châu (2004). Phương ngữ học tiếng Việt [Vietnamese dialectology]. Hà Nội: Nhà xuất bản Đại học Quốc gia Hà Nội.
Vũ, Thanh Phương (1982). Phonetic properties of Vietnamese tones across dialects. In David Bradley (ed.), Papers in South-East Asian Linguistics 8: Tonation. Pacific Linguistics.
Phạm, Ben & McLeod, Sharynne (2016). Consonants, vowels and tones across Vietnamese dialects. International Journal of Speech-Language Pathology 18(2).
Kirby, James P. (2011). Vietnamese (Hanoi Vietnamese). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 41(3), 381-392.
Kirby, James (2010). Dialect experience in Vietnamese tone perception. Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 127(6).
contrasts: five tones: hỏi and ngã are one tone
retroflex ʈ ʂ ʐ (written tr, s, r) against palatal c, alveolar s and the glide j (written ch, x, d or gi); Hanoi has lost these contrasts
implosive ɓ ɗ against voiceless unaspirated t, k and aspirated tʰ
long against short a and ɤ in closed syllables
final alveolars and velars are merged: written n and t are said as ŋ and k after most vowels
allophony: written d and gi are the glide [j]
written r is a retroflex fricative or approximant [ʐ ~ ɻ], sometimes a tap or trill
written v is [v]; [j], the Southern value, is also heard
final written n and t are velar [ŋ], [k̚] after most vowels (ăn is [ʔaŋ])
final p t k are unreleased
after rounded vowels final k and ŋ are labial-velar, as in the other dialects
a syllable written with an initial vowel begins with a glottal stop
syllable_structure: (C)(w)V(C) plus tone; the coda is one of p t k m n ŋ or a glide j, w
phonotactics: syllables ending in a stop carry only the sắc or the nặng tone
the short vowels occur only in closed syllables

stress.rule: The last syllable of a phrase is the most prominent; grammatical words are weaker.
stress.cues: duration, intensity and fuller realisation of the tone contour

length.notes: Length is contrastive only for a against ă and ɤ against ɤ̆, in closed syllables.

intonation.declarative: lexical tones are kept within a low, compressed range; mild declination
intonation.yes_no_question: marked by particles (không, and local forms such as hỉ and hả); register raised
intonation.wh_question: question word in place (local forms chi, mô, răng, rứa); often a final particle
intonation.notes: No instrumental study of Huế intonation is known to the compiler; entries are general and of low confidence.

tone.confidence_notes: Published descriptions of Huế tones disagree in detail and the Chao digits below are the ones most often repeated in comparative tables, not the result of one instrumental study. What is agreed: five tones, hỏi and ngã merged, a low and narrow pitch range, ngang the highest tone, sắc low rather than high rising.

inventory.name: ngang, high rising in Huế; no tone mark
espeak_aliases: 7 (used on the last stressed syllable of a clause)
inventory.description: The highest tone; mid to high, rising.

inventory.name: huyền, mid level in Huế; grave accent
sắc, low rising in Huế; acute accent
inventory.description: Low with a small rise, the reverse of the high rising sắc of Hanoi and Saigon; glottalisation is reported.

inventory.name: hỏi and ngã (merged), low falling; hook above and tilde
espeak_aliases: 5 (ngã, which eSpeak NG keeps as a separate tone phoneme with almost the same contour)
inventory.description: Falls from mid to low with at most a slight final rise. Words written with hỏi and with ngã are said alike.

inventory.name: nặng, low dipping; dot below
inventory.description: Low fall with a slight final rise; heavy, with glottalisation reported.

sandhi: no categorical tone sandhi; gradient tonal coarticulation only
tone.notes: Listeners from other regions find Huế tones hard to identify because the contours lie close together in a low range (compare Kirby 2010 on dialect experience). No absolute F0 values are given here.

phonation: glottalisation reported on nặng and sắc

problems: no sentence intonation and no declination: CalcPitches_Tone() in src/libespeak-ng/intonation.c ignores the clause type, and a question gives the same audio as a statement

the tones are crowded into a very small range: with the voice setting 'pitch 82 118' everything lies between about 73 and 100 Hz, and huyền, sắc, hỏi, ngã and nặng all lie between about 73 and 85 Hz (under 3 semitones, measured on the output), so they are hard to tell apart
written s is the plain alveolar s, the same as x, so the retroflex ʂ is missing, although tr and r do get retroflex phonemes (cr, z.)
several vowels (i, E, a:, @, @:, O) are reset to a fixed length of 150 in ph_vietnam_hue, which removes the coda-dependent durations of the Northern table
voice quality is not modelled; glottalisation is imitated only by a dip in amplitude (envelope vi_6amp, used on huyền, ngã and nặng)
no tonal coarticulation, and a pause between all words ('words 1')
good: the tone table is redefined for Huế and follows the pattern in the literature: ngang is a rise and the highest tone, huyền a mid level, sắc a very low tone, hỏi and ngã two nearly identical low falls (the merger), nặng a fall with a slight rise
final written n and t are turned into velars, and d and gi into a palatal fricative close to [j]
tr and ch, and r and d, are kept apart

notes: The voice selects its rules with 'dictrules 1' and its sounds with the phoneme table vi-hue, which inherits from vi. eSpeak NG tone numbers are the same as for Northern Vietnamese (1 ngang, 2 huyền, 3 sắc, 4 hỏi, 5 ngã, 6 nặng, 7 clause-final ngang) with different contours.
